title: API Reference
markdown:
The FastAPI surface lives in `openexecutive.api.main`, which mounts one router per topic. A shared-secret middleware gates every request via an `x-api-key` header, except `/health` and the `/webhook/*` callbacks (which carry their own verification). With local login (`OE_LOCAL_LOGIN=1`, which only `make dev` sets, and only while neither Google nor SSO sign-in is set up) a second middleware answers 403 to any request whose raw `Host` is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (except a webhook that verifies its caller: Google Chat always, Telegram only with a `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` Telegram can send), and to any write whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is present and not `same-origin`/`none`. The UI signs that owner in with no password and this API usually has no secret, so without it a web page in the owner's browser could drive the API as the principal — by DNS-rebinding its own hostname to 127.0.0.1, or by posting a plain form from another site or localhost port. CORS is restricted to configured UI origins. The gate is off when `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` is unset — intended for local development only — so any internet-reachable deployment sets `OE_PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT`, and `create_app()` then refuses to boot without the secret rather than serving an unauthenticated API.

**Who is calling** is read in one place, `api/caller.py`, which answers with a `Caller` kind and email; a test fails on any other read of an `x-caller-*` header. By default (`open`) it is the `x-caller-email` the UI proxy stamps from the sign-in, trusted because whoever holds the shared secret is trusted as the proxy, and a request with none runs as the principal. **Signed callers** remove that trust. With `CALLER_ASSERTION_PUBLIC_KEYS` set, the proxy signs every request with an Ed25519 key only the UI holds, and a third middleware checks the `x-caller-assertion` header:

- **What it covers.** It is good for one method, the exact path and query, at most 120 seconds, and one use. The API keeps used ids in memory.
- **What it names.** A `user`, by email, or the `operator`: local login, which runs as the principal.
- **No caller header at all** is a `service`, for scripts or MCP clients holding only the secret. It is never the principal, not even on an install with no owner yet, so it can't save a first setup.
- **Anything else is a 401.** That includes an `x-caller-email` without an assertion (`caller_assertion_required`), and a bad, expired, reused or mismatched assertion (`caller_assertion_invalid`).

Public keys that can't be read stop the boot, rather than fall back to trusting the header. `scripts/make-caller-keys.py` makes the pair, and `scripts/mint-caller-assertion.py` signs one request for curl. The API holds only public keys. Setup's API-protection check warns while a shared secret is set without them.

Endpoints grouped by router:

| Router | Key endpoints | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `POST /chat`, `POST /chat/stop`, `POST /chat/add` | SSE stream of a live Executive turn. `POST /chat/add` hands the running turn a message the person typed while it works; the turn takes it at its next step and the stream names it in a `message_added` event, and a second `POST /chat` on the same conversation waits for the first to finish. The request body optionally carries `page_context` (route, page title, guide section id, and a form descriptor with current values) — sent only by the Ask OE side panel so the Executive can explain the current page or propose form values. When the Executive calls its `propose_form_values` tool, the stream emits a `form_patch` event (`{type, form_id, fields, rationale, iteration}`) that the panel applies into the on-screen form as highlighted suggestions; the user reviews and saves through the form's normal submit path. Each round of tool calls also emits an `activity` event (`{type, label, tool, iteration}`) naming what is running — progress only, forwarded verbatim and never persisted with the message, unlike an `action_taken` chip. A `session_id` in the body must be a chat the caller may use (the same ownership rule as `sessions`). If it isn't, the turn runs in a fresh chat instead, so nothing is written into someone else's session and the reply looks the same as for an unknown id. An unknown namespaced id (`slack:…`, `telegram:…` and so on) is ignored and a fresh chat is started, because those ids belong to the channel adapters and claiming one first would make the caller its owner. The client mints a `client_turn_id` and sends it with the turn; `POST /chat/stop` takes that id and halts the turn mid-flight, so the button is live from the moment Send is pressed rather than only once the first SSE byte arrives. A stopped turn emits a `stopped` event and then the usual `done` over the same still-open stream — never an `error` — and whatever streamed so far is persisted and flagged. The endpoint returns 404 both for an unknown id and for another caller's turn, so it cannot be used to probe which turns are live. An optional `memory_text` (1–2000 chars) is what peer memory records as the caller's words instead of `message` — the briefing handoffs send it because their seed quotes the Executive's own card; `POST /chat/upload` derives it from the typed text and filenames. Since it never reaches the transcript, the `chat_turn` audit row keeps it beside `message`. After the reply — a stopped or timed-out one too, before the `stopped` / `error` / `done` frames — a turn that looked at anything sends one `sources` event, `{type, session_id, sources: [{kind, title, url}], unavailable: [area]}`: `kind` is `company`, `knowledge`, `notion`, `research`, `document` or `web`, `url` is only ever an http(s) link or, for an earlier document, `/artifacts/<id>`, at most 12 sources (6 from the web, pages the reply cites first), and `unavailable` names parts of the analysis ("finance") whose specialist failed or said nothing every time it was asked. It is persisted with the reply as `chat_messages.sources`. A request that carries `x-caller-email` marks its turn signed in (`Session.web_caller_signed_in`), which Act as me needs on a deployment without local login. |
| `sessions` | `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{id}`, `GET /sessions/{id}/messages`, `DELETE /sessions/{id}`, `POST /sessions/{id}/messages/{message_id}/feedback`, `GET /sessions/{id}/followup` | List, read and delete saved chat sessions (assistant messages carry their row `id` and any `feedback`). The list is scoped to the caller. Every per-session route checks ownership, because session ids are guessable (`slack:dm:<user id>`, `telegram:<chat id>`): only the session's owner or the principal gets through, and a legacy row with no owner is the principal's alone. Anyone else gets the same 404 as for an unknown id, so the routes can't be used to find out which chats exist. The one other way in is having started the chat in this process (matched by Person id or verified email, so it survives the caller being added to the roster), which is how a caller the roster can't resolve keeps using their own chat. That record is in memory, so after a restart such an ownerless chat is refused for reads. The principal can continue someone else's ownerless chat without becoming its owner. Deleting a session also drops its in-memory copy, so a later turn naming that id starts fresh. The feedback route records 👍/👎 (`{"feedback": "up"|"down"|null}`) on one assistant reply; only the session's own caller or the principal may rate it. The rater is stored (`feedback_by_person_id`), and a 👎 on a reply to the rater's own message triggers a working-style pass for them (paced; see attunement). The chat stream's `done` event carries `message_id` for the persisted reply. The followup route returns `{"suggestion": string|null}` — one suggested next user message, written by the utility-fast model from the last few turns, that the chat composer shows as its greyed placeholder (Tab / → or the inline chip fills it in without sending). It is null unless the session ends on a persisted assistant reply, and null (uncached) when the model fails. Same ownership check as feedback; successful suggestions are cached in-process per (session, reply id). Messages from `GET /sessions/{id}/messages` carry each assistant reply's saved `sources` (the same shape as the chat stream's `sources` event, without `type`), so a reloaded chat shows them again. |
| `today` | `GET /today`, `GET /today/activity`, `GET /today/activity/daily`, `GET /today/brief-delivery`, `GET /today/top-three`, `GET /today/weekly-review` | Morning-brief aggregation, recent-action rail, and Pulse heartbeat heatmap (per-day activity counts). `GET /today` carries the viewer's cached "What's going on" `narrative` with `narrative_generated_at` (when it was written) and `narrative_stale` (a fresher one is being written — the page re-polls; see Today). A proposal backed by a roster request carries `roster_request` (the new sender's server-derived details and held-message previews; the principal's only) and is answered through the `people` routes below. `brief-delivery` returns the latest morning brief or end-of-day digest that didn't reach the owner, as `{brief, at, problem, fix, readable}` in plain language (`readable` is false when it couldn't be written, so there is nothing to read), or null — null while briefs go out, once the cause is fixed, while the scheduler is off, and for anyone but the owner (`chat._caller_is_principal_or_unclaimed`); it carries no address or channel id. `top-three` and `weekly-review` feed the solo Briefing's own cards and answer only in solo mode and only to the principal (`workflows._caller_is_the_principal`: a principal match or no caller header, never an unclaimed roster); anyone else, and team mode, get null. `top-three` returns `{items: [{key, kind, text, why, slot}]}` — the morning brief's top three from the same code (`build_top_three(principal_due_soon())`), `slot` a free block like `10:00–11:00`, `""` when none is left, null when no calendar was read — and is kept off `GET /today` because its calendar read may take up to 4 s. `weekly-review` returns the latest completed `weekly_review` run as `{run_id, completed_at, period, top_three, excerpt}` (next week's top three as plain text; `excerpt` when that list is empty), or null when none has completed. |
| `people` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH /people`, `POST /people/{id}/archive`, `GET /people/requests`, `GET /people/requests/{id}`, `POST /people/requests/{id}/approve`, `POST /people/requests/{id}/decline`, `GET\|POST /people/{id}/open-loops`, `POST /open-loops/{loop_id}/close`, `GET /people/{id}/outreach`, `GET\|PUT\|DELETE /people/{id}/attunement` | Roster CRUD and scope lookups. Every `Person` carries `kind` (`team` / `contact`). `GET /people` lists team members only unless `?include_contacts=true` (the People page asks for both; the department-head and workflow pickers keep the default); `POST` / `PATCH` accept `kind`, and a principal contact is a 422 either way. They also take `email_aliases` (other addresses the person writes from, at most 10; on `PATCH` the full list replaces the current one, omitted leaves it): an alias matches their mail and may be emailed but never signs in; a malformed one is a 422, and an alias — or a new primary `email` — that is already someone else's address or alias is a 409. Every `POST` / `PATCH` then closes any pending roster request whose sender now matches someone and replays its held messages. Adding, editing and archiving (`POST`, `PATCH`, `/archive`) are the principal's only, or anyone's while no one is principal yet so a first setup can add its owner (`chat._caller_is_principal_or_unclaimed`, the check behind `PUT /workspace`; a request with no `x-caller-email`, such as the CLI or local login, counts as the principal). Anyone else, a person editing their own row included, gets 403 before the person lookup, so it can't probe which ids exist. Contacts are private to the principal (`caller_is_principal`: the signed-in email is the principal's, or no `x-caller-email`; stricter than the owner rule above, so while no one is principal nobody is): for anyone else `include_contacts` is ignored, a contact's id is a 404 on `GET /people/{id}` and open-loops (exactly as for a missing id; `PATCH` and archive are already a 403 for them), and creating a contact or turning someone into one is a 403, even on a first setup with no principal yet. `GET /people/me` returns `{person_id, is_principal}` so the UI offers contacts to the principal only. `GET /people/by-scope/{token}` never returns a contact. Archiving a person closes their open loops. The open-loop routes list what a person owes (soonest due first) and close one (`reason`: done / not_needed / cancelled) — both the principal's or the owner's only (403 otherwise, via `people.store.is_principal_or_self`). `POST /people/{id}/open-loops` `{task, due_date?}` assigns that person a task (201 with the loop; `due_date` is a local date, due 17:00 in the user's timezone, clamped to 60 days, default 2 days): any active team member may assign anyone on the team, 403 for anyone else; 409 for an archived person, a contact (as seen by the principal), a person at the open-loop cap, a duplicate or open loops turned off; 422 for an empty task. Nobody is messaged at assignment — the owner is chased once it is due. `/outreach` returns, per kind of proactive outreach over 30 days, `sent` / `replied` / `acted` / `ignored` / `pending` (voided DMs are excluded) — same access rule, checked before the person lookup so it can't probe which ids exist. `/attunement` reads, replaces (`rules`: up to 4 strings, or omitted to only set `locked`) or resets the person's working-style rules — same access rule, 404 for an archived person; `PUT` rejects a rule that is not purely about style with 422. Archiving a person also drops their working style and frees their aliases. The **roster-request** routes (declared before `/people/{person_id}`) are the principal's alone (`caller_is_principal`; anyone else gets 404, as for a missing id): `GET /people/requests?status=pending|approved|linked|declined|expired|superseded|all` lists up to 100 (`id`, `channel`, `channel_ref`, sanitised `display_name`, `profile_email`, `on_company_domain`, `suggested_kind`, `suggested_person_id` / `_name`, `status`, `resolved_person_id` / `_kind`, `message_count`, timestamps, `ack_sent`, and `previews` of the held messages while pending — shown to the principal, never to a model); `approve` takes either `link_person_id` (+ `replace_channel_id`) or `full_name` + `kind` (no default: 422 without both) + optional `role`; `decline` takes no body. An answered request is a 409, a chat id or address already on someone else is a 409; the held messages are replayed (or dropped) in the background. |
| `departments` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /departments`, `.../goals` | Department state and per-department goals. `PATCH /departments/{slug}` also takes `watched_entities` (≤50 names, `[]` clears) — the entities the research watch policy may add watches for and route to this department. A `cadences` spec that does not parse is rejected with a 422 (empty means no cadence). A new `head_person_id` must be a team member: an unknown id and one of the principal's contacts get the same name-free 422 (`person_id N is not on the team.`), so the route — open to any signed-in user — never reveals that a contact exists; an unchanged head is not re-checked. `POST .../goals` requires only `key_result`: a missing or blank `period_value` is filled with the current period for `period_type` in the user's zone (the same label `create_goal` uses), and `target` defaults to empty. `PATCH .../goals/{id}` rejects a blank `key_result` or `period_value` with a 422; `target` may be cleared. |
| `agents` | `GET /agents`, `GET /agents/models`, `GET /agents/models/options`, `GET /agents/presets`, `POST /agents/presets/{id}`, `PATCH /agents/{id}`, `POST /agents/{id}/test` | Specialist metadata and Council overrides. `/agents/models` is the flat model allowlist the PATCH validator uses; `/agents/models/options` returns the same ids in the same order, each tagged with `provider`, `provider_label`, `route` (`direct` / `openrouter` / `local`) and a display `label`, for the Council's Provider → Model picker. `AgentDetail` carries `instructions` (additional instructions, appended after `prompt`, which stays the built-in prompt or its replacement); `PATCH` and `/test` accept `instructions` (max 4,000 chars, blank clears it). `GET /agents/presets` lists the Fast, Balanced and Thorough quality presets (each with `available` and the resolved `model` for this install) plus `active` (null when the council is Custom), `base` and `custom_agents`; `POST /agents/presets/{id}` applies one by writing per-agent model and deep-reasoning overrides and returns the same shape (404 unknown preset, 409 when the install allows none of its models). Each `AgentMeta` carries `visibility` (`core` or `internal`) so the Council's simple view can list core agents first. |
| `personas` | `GET\|PUT\|POST\|DELETE /personas` | Executive persona definitions. |
| `alerts` | `POST /alerts/{id}/ack`, `POST /alerts/bulk-ack`, `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen`, `POST /alerts/review` | Groom the briefing queue. `ack` (`read`/`ack`/`dismissed`, optional `mute_topic`) also teaches a watch-sourced alert's watch (`trust_score`); `bulk-ack` takes explicit `alert_ids` and/or `older_than_days` + `category` (exempt sources skipped); `reopen` is the Undo for a `resolved` / `expired` / `dismissed` alert (never `ack` or an artifact / decision row; back to `unread` with every review stamp cleared and its TTL anchor refreshed, so it is live again even if older than its TTL); `review` runs the Executive's relevance review on demand (ignores the interval; still honours `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED`, the per-pass caps, the single-flight lock and per-alert idempotency) and returns the move counts. `bulk-ack` caps ids at 500, needs `older_than_days >= 1`, and applies watch feedback per row; `mute_topic` must be one of the alert's tags or a scoped `external:` / `department:` pattern. Alerts still surface only through the briefing (`/today` reads the live view) — there is no list, prefs, mutes, or live-stream endpoint. |
| `artifacts` | `GET /artifacts`, `GET /artifacts/{id}`, `GET /artifacts/{id}/download?as=`, `POST /artifacts/{id}/archive`, `POST /artifacts/{id}/restore`, `DELETE /artifacts/{id}` | Browsable deliverables in any format — Markdown, HTML, Word, Excel, or a link into a connected app — with `format`, `downloads`, `external_url` and `supersedes_id` on every summary. `download` renders the file (Word/Excel built at request time from the stored text; any Markdown artifact, workflow output included, can export `?as=docx`) and is always an attachment with `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. Every route answers for the signed-in caller (`artifact_records.Viewer`): a drafted artifact is its owner's alone (`alerts.owner_person_id`, the person whose conversation published it; none = the principal's), a workflow output follows its run (`persistence.run_visible_to`), and anything the caller may not see is a 404 like a missing id, the principal included. `POST /alerts/{id}/ack` and `/reopen` answer 404 for someone else's drafted artifact the same way. |
| `decisions` | `GET /decisions`, `POST /decisions/{id}/{approve,reject,cancel}`, `GET`/`PUT /decisions/classes/meeting_scheduling`, `GET /audit/reliability` | Approval-gated decision instances (e.g. calendar bookings). What approve/reject/cancel do is per class (`DECISION_CLASSES`, one `DecisionClassSpec` each; meeting booking books on approve and deletes on cancel; `delegation_reply`, an inbox reply card, is its approver's alone (`approver_only`) — hidden from everyone else, the principal included when it is a team member's — sends its Gmail draft on approve and, after a reject, deletes the draft unless it was edited), and an instance of a class with no spec gets 409 instead of being carried out as another. Only the principal, or the person the decision went to for approval (`approver_person_id`), may approve, reject or cancel it. Anyone else gets 403, and a decision nobody was asked about, or one private to the principal, is the principal's alone. The resolver is recorded as `resolver_person_id`, and a reject that loses the race to another answer is a 409. `GET /audit/reliability` is the principal's alone (403 otherwise), because it counts private decisions too. A proposed booking is surfaced on the briefing as a companion alert; approve/reject/cancel here also clear that alert. An approval whose caller resolves to the principal runs the booking inside `grant_contact_egress()`, so a meeting the principal proposed with a contact can be created. Such a booking's payload is marked `private`: it is proposed to the principal, left out of anyone else's `GET /decisions`, and a 404 for them on `GET /decisions/{id}` and every action route. Reviewed in the briefing — there is no separate proposals page. The class routes read and set how meetings are handled: both return `{decision_class: "meeting_scheduling", mode: "propose" \| "auto_execute"}` (default `propose`); the `PUT` body is `{mode}`, principal-only (403 otherwise, open before a principal exists — but then only `propose` can be set: `auto_execute` is a 409 until a non-archived principal is on the roster), 422 on any other mode, and a change writes a `decision_class_mode_changed` audit row. In solo mode the class mode decides a booking, and `auto_execute` applies only to a turn the principal started on a verified surface — any other turn gets a proposal. |
| `delegation` | `GET`/`PUT /delegation`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /delegation/voice`, `POST /delegation/voice/learn`, `POST /delegation/voice/describe`, `POST /delegation/voice/signature`, `PUT /delegation/inbox`, `POST /delegation/inbox/check`, `GET /delegation/replies`, `PUT /delegation/handle-it`, `GET /delegation/handled`, `PUT /delegation/team` | Act as me — the **caller's own** delegation only; nobody sets it for anyone else. It answers the principal, and a team member once the owner lets them; anyone else gets 403 `not_available_yet`. `GET /delegation` returns `{enabled, gmail: {status, message, email, connect_command, outlook_connect_command, provider}, inbox: {enabled, status, message, watch_since, last_poll_at, checking}, handle_it: {enabled, mode, available, sent_today}, team}`, where `team` is the owner's switch for the principal while `DELEGATION_TEAM_MEMBERS` allows it — `{enabled, members: [{person_id, name, enabled, inbox, drafts_30d, sent_30d}]}`, counts only — and `null` otherwise. `PUT /delegation/handle-it` takes `{enabled?, mode?}` (`mode` is `careful`, `balanced` or `bold`; anything else is a 422 `bad_mode`) from a caller the API knows is that person — 403 `not_yours`, 409 `caller_signing_required` with only the shared secret — and turning it on needs Act as me and Draft replies to my inbox on (409 `act_as_me_off` / `inbox_off`); `GET /delegation/handled` returns `{replies: [{decision_id, sent_at, to_name, to_email, subject, body, open_questions, gmail_link, source}]}`, the caller's replies and follow-ups (`source` `follow_up`) sent on its own in the last 7 days; a card on `GET /delegation/replies` carries `source` the same way. `PUT /delegation/team` takes `{enabled}` from the principal alone (403 `principal_only`; 409 `not_available` when the install doesn't allow it). The Gmail `status` is `connected`, `not_configured`, `needs_reconnect`, `mismatch`, `no_email`, `shared_mailbox` or `error`, checked live with Google on each call. `PUT` takes `{enabled}` (any other field is a 422); turning it on needs the caller's own Gmail connected, otherwise a 409 whose code says why (`gmail_not_connected`, `gmail_needs_reconnect`, `gmail_mismatch`, `no_email`, `shared_mailbox`, `gmail_error`). The voice routes show, learn (from the caller's sent mail, one pass at a time — a 409 `in_progress`, `locked`, `too_soon`, `not_enough_mail`, `no_profile` or `changed` when it was locked or edited while learning, or a Gmail code), write it from the caller's own description (`POST /delegation/voice/describe` with `{description}`: one model call applies their words to the profile they have and returns it with a short `sample_reply`, saving nothing, so they review it and save it with `PUT`; a 409 `empty`, `too_long`, `in_progress`, `too_many` past 10 an hour or `no_profile`; no mailbox needed), edit and lock, and reset "How I write": a typed field that fails validation is a 422 `invalid_voice` listing each `rejected` field, and `clear_exemplars` / `clear_signature` drop those. `POST /delegation/voice/signature` reads the signature from the caller's Gmail settings again and changes nothing else (a locked profile stays locked), with the same Gmail codes as learning: a 409 when their mailbox isn't connected, it refuses the sign-in or the check itself fails (`gmail_error`), and a 502 `gmail_error` when reading the signature fails. On an Outlook mailbox it is a 409 `signature_unavailable`, since Outlook gives apps no signature to read, and the stored one is left alone. A caller `can_delegate` refuses — anyone but the principal, for now — gets 403 `not_available_yet`, which hides the Settings card. A request with no `x-caller-email` is a 403 `sign_in_required` unless the API runs under local login — a header-less call is not a sign-in (the caller is read through `api/caller.py`, as on every principal-only route). `PUT /delegation/inbox` takes `{enabled}` and turns **Draft replies to my inbox** on or off, returning the same shape as `GET /delegation`: on needs Act as me on (409 `act_as_me_off`) and the mailbox connected (the Gmail codes above, which keep their names for an Outlook mailbox too), and turning Act as me off turns it off too. `POST /delegation/inbox/check` starts a scan now in the background and answers 202 with the `inbox` state (409 `inbox_off` or `in_progress`). `GET /delegation/replies` returns `{cards: [...]}`, the caller's open reply cards from the database alone (no Gmail call): the decision id, the sender's name, address, relation and whether it was verified, the subject, when it arrived, what they wrote, the draft's recipients, subject and body, `open_questions`, `flags` and a Gmail link built from a fixed prefix. **Send** is `POST /decisions/{id}/approve`: it sends the card's draft exactly as it is in Gmail, after checking again that the caller is its owner — which on a server needs signed callers (409 `caller_signing_required` otherwise) — that both switches are on (`inbox_off`), no client slot is active (`client_slot`), the Gmail is connected (the Gmail codes), the draft is still there and unanswered (`draft_gone`, `you_replied`) and its recipients are allowed (`no_recipients`, `too_many_recipients`, `executive_recipient`, `not_from_you`). Recipients that changed, or a newer message in the thread, answer 409 `{code: "confirm", message, reasons, recipients}`; approving again with `edits: {recipients: <the list shown>, thread_moved_on: true}` is the second yes. A draft edited in Gmail between those checks and the send is not sent (`draft_changed`). A double tap sends once (`already_handled`); Gmail refusing answers 429 `rate_limited` or 502 `gmail_error` with nothing sent, and a send Gmail didn't confirm answers 502 `send_unconfirmed` and is settled by the next inbox scan. Dismiss is `POST /decisions/{id}/reject`. Every change writes a private audit row. |
| `history` | `GET /memories/history` (`?q=`), `PUT /memories/history/settings`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /memories/history/{id}`, `POST /memories/history/{id}/forget-conversation` | Always in the loop: the **caller's own** notes and switches only, resolved as for Act as me (a signed-in person on the roster, or the principal under local login; otherwise 403 `sign_in_required` / `not_on_roster`). `GET` returns `{notes, reply_notes, retention_days, effective_retention_days, company_retention_days, retention_choices, can_keep_notes, can_note_replies, can_set_company_retention}` (`can_keep_notes`: a team member on the People list may turn notes on; `can_note_replies`: they can use Act as me, so email replies are noted too). `PUT` turns notes on only for someone who may keep them (403 `not_available`), takes a person's retention only when shorter than the company's (422 `invalid_setting`), and the company retention only from the principal (403 `principal_only`). `PATCH` pins or corrects a note; `DELETE` forgets it; `forget-conversation` is "Don't remember this". A note that isn't the caller's is 404. Every change is audited privately to its person. |
| `audit` | `GET /audit/logs`, `GET /audit/logs/{id}`, `GET /audit/sessions/{id}`, `GET /audit/usage`, `POST /audit/log` | Durable audit trail of side effects. `/audit/sessions/{id}` adds a per-session token cost summary; `/audit/usage` aggregates token usage and OpenRouter cost across all sessions (totals, by day, by model, and by source — the part of the system that made the calls — including server-side web-search counts). Rows private to the principal (`private_to_principal`: a turn about their private mail, or a row naming one of their contacts on their own turn) are theirs alone: for any other caller, resolved as for `/alerts`, the list, its `total` and the usage totals leave them out, a private row's id is a 404, and a session shows only its other rows. |
| `architecture` | `GET /architecture/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | This documentation surface. |
